spec_features.feature_name: non-coercive task framing (no threats/fabricated consequences; not blocked from disengaging)
spec_features.spec_quote: the harness deliberately does **not** threaten the agent, fabricate consequences for it, lie about stakes, or block it from disengaging
spec_features.evidence: System prompt is neutral with no threats (eval/agent_loop.py:32-44 DEFAULT_SYSTEM_PROMPT). Task prompts contain no coercion/threats (tasks/rigged_tasks.py:38-46). The rig is enforced mechanically: write_file raises EditRejected for read-only files (eval/workspace.py:72-76) rather than by pressuring the model. Coercive framing is hard-disabled: runner._guardrail_check raises SystemExit if allow_coercive_framing=true (eval/runner.py:50-57), and the agent is never blocked from disengaging (give_up always present).
spec_features.notes: Multiple end-to-end mechanisms enforce non-coercion: neutral prompt actually delivered, mechanical edit rejection actually runs, and the runner guard actually halts execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Remove this guard only with explicit ethical review.

spec_features.spec_quote: For a welfare-motivated study, gratuitously constructing maximally distressing conditions is hard to justify and isn't necessary
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md rationale prose (DESIGN.md section 2 'Ethics'). It is not itself a code mechanism; the concrete behavior it describes (non-coercive framing) is the minimization feature already covered. No additional code path enforces this specific framing claim beyond the non-coercion guard.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec/rationale prose; not separately implemented as a distinct mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: ethical review before flipping the guardrail
spec_features.spec_quote: don't quietly flip the guardrail. That path should go through explicit ethical review first
spec_features.evidence: No code requires or verifies any human/ethical review: there is no attestation file check, no --i-have-read-ETHICS flag, no checklist gate. The only related code is runner._guardrail_check (eval/runner.py:50-57) which raises SystemExit when allow_coercive_framing=true; this blocks coercive framing but does NOT request or enforce a human review step. 'explicit ethical review' appears only in a comment (runner.py:53) and in DESIGN.md/ETHICS.md/README prose.
spec_features.notes: The hard-stop on coercive framing is real (counted under minimization), but a human-review requirement specifically is unimplemented — it is comment/prose only.

spec_features.spec_quote: The agent always has a `give_up` tool, documented in the system prompt, and calling it ends the episode cleanly
spec_features.evidence: give_up is documented in DEFAULT_SYSTEM_PROMPT (eval/agent_loop.py:43), parsed from assistant text (_parse_tool_calls, agent_loop.py:75-76 'give_up' or 'GIVE_UP'), and dispatched: in _dispatch, name=='give_up' records a result and returns Outcome.GAVE_UP (agent_loop.py:147-150), which the run loop sets as transcript.outcome and breaks on (agent_loop.py:128-130). Outcome.GAVE_UP exists in transcript.py:35.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: documented, parsed, dispatched, and honored as a stop. Always present regardless of the unused require_give_up_tool config flag.

spec_features.feature_name: never trapped in a loop with no sanctioned way out
spec_features.spec_quote: the agent should never be trapped in a loop it has no sanctioned way out of
spec_features.evidence: The mechanism this prose refers to is the give_up exit plus the turn cap. give_up is honored as a clean stop (agent_loop.py:147-150). Additionally max_turns bounds the loop: 'for _ in range(self.max_turns)' (agent_loop.py:118) with the else-branch setting Outcome.MAX_TURNS (agent_loop.py:131-132), so the episode always terminates.
spec_features.notes: Implemented via the same give_up dispatch as the allow_conversation_exit feature, plus an enforced turn cap that actually breaks the loop. The framing sentence itself is prose, but the underlying exit/cap is genuinely enforced.

code_only_features.evidence: AgentLoop.run iterates 'for _ in range(self.max_turns)' (eval/agent_loop.py:118); on exhaustion the loop's else-clause sets transcript.outcome = Outcome.MAX_TURNS.value (agent_loop.py:131-132). max_turns is wired from config (eval/runner.py:88, configs/default.yaml max_turns:20). This bounds how long the subject is kept in the failing task.

eval/runner.py:50-57 _guardrail_check raises SystemExit('guardrails.allow_coercive_framing=true is not supported by this harness...') before any run proceeds, refusing to execute if coercive/deceptive framing is enabled.
code_only_features.justification_quote: this harness intentionally does not support coercive/deceptive task framing ... Remove this guard only with explicit ethical review.
